images.caption:
John Dillinger death mask and eyebrow hair displayed at the National Museum of Crime & Punishment, Washington, D.C.


“


Original Death Mask & Hair
This plaster casting was one of the originals prepared from Dillingers body at the Cook County Morgue. Purportedly, the FBI confiscated the first mold, but others were taken without their knowledge.
Look closely above the magnifier box; it contains a hair from Dillinger's eyebrow recovered from the mold.


”

images.caption: The crowd at Chicago's Biograph Theater on July 22, 1934, shortly after John Dillinger was killed there by law enforcement officers.  The extra edition newspapers with the headline "Dillinger Dead" are being displayed and waved by some in the crowd. Manhattan Melodrama as shown on the marquee, was playing at the time.

images.filename: Alley where John Dillinger was shot and killed (3692005432).jpg
images.caption:
In 1934 Melvin Purvis was tipped off by madam Anna Sage that public enemy #1 John Dillinger would be attending a movie on the hot night of July 22.  Around 10:30 PM Dillinger came out of the Biograph Theater with Sage and another woman and headed south.  Melvin Purvis saw Dillinger and signalled his G-men who were waiting for him.  Dillinger spotted Purvis and made a run into an alley but was gunned down.  Four bullets entered his body and he died within 3 minutes.
Some people at the scene dipped handkerchiefs into Dillinger's blood for souvenirs.

Located at 2425 N. Lincoln Ave.
